conflicts.text: Orb colors ROTATE for Creating/Shares/Comments — Playbook map (Creating orange #ff9a5a, Shares green #2fe89e, Comments gold #ffbf3d) vs live dashboard code (CREATIONS green #2fe89e, SHARES gold #ffbf3d, COMMENTS orange #ff9a5a). Recorded, NOT resolved — Shawn’s eye. Touches piece 05.

Notes orb is #3fb8ff in BOTH the Playbook and the live code. The working record’s #3a5bff appears in neither source as the ORB color — use #3fb8ff. Nuance found by this harvest: #3a5bff DOES appear in harvested/dashboard.html as the notes accent in the notes drill-down (L4470–4481, L6104–6160, L12881, L12903, L14856) — a later-build usage, not the orb. Do not use #3a5bff for the orb. Touches piece 05.
Act §4.2 says board radius 24px (Design Laws Law 3); the Hub ships 26px (hub.html:1176). Unresolved — Shawn’s eye. Touches piece 02.
Naya Design Contract V1 EXISTS, but no file says “NIA Design Contract” — whether V1 IS the document Shawn means is Shawn’s word, not decided here. Touches distribution, not a piece.

pieces.name: Button — the one button
pieces.check: CHECK: center #050505; white text + icon; border ≥1.5px white at rest; touch ≥44px (principal CTA ≥52px); focus + pressed states present. A flat button fails.
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary button: one DNA, really black, white-rimmed at rest, igniting in its own color — molded to be the single action a person trusts without reading.
pieces.notes: CSS verbatim; specimen is usage of the verbatim class names (dashboard button markup is JS-rendered, so no verbatim static markup exists to copy).

pieces.name: Board — the outer board
pieces.check: CHECK: 5-layer shadow values present; border 1.5px; radius 24px (hub ships 26px — see note); a board that blends into the field fails.
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary board: one slab per thing, obsidian, tone-spined, jewel-cornered — molded to hold a whole world at one glance and open it on touch.
pieces.notes: NOTE: the Act says radius 24px (Design Laws Law 3); the Hub ships border-radius 26px (hub.html:1176). Reported, not resolved — Act CONFLICTS territory, Shawn's eye decides.

pieces.name: Intelligent block — the grand block
pieces.check: CHECK: each inner layer visibly lifted off the outer board; each lit in its own icon color; nutshell text 20px white; no voice; no flat lighter box. CHECK: his eye on whether it is the grand block.
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary block: the grand block, elevation upon elevation, every voice of one intelligence — molded to tell the truth so anyone understands it.
pieces.notes: Structure verbatim from the render code (hub.html:5747-5845: el() calls build exactly these classes; layer head is a <button> with aria-expanded; deeper tiers start closed/hidden). Layer jewel colors live in layerColorFor / LAYER_COLORS (JS, hub.html) — see companion law §5. The .ib-layer-play voice button exists in code but the law forbids voice on the board — it is NOT harvested here.

pieces.name: Icon — drawn, not shrunk
pieces.check: CHECK: readable at 16px; a beautiful but inert affordance fails. CHECK: his eye on whether the glyph keeps its promise.
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary icon: drawn, not shrunk, a faceted jewel readable at 16px — molded to say what a thing is and promise what it does.
pieces.notes: v10 faceted jewel icon: SVG with .core / .facet / .shade / .edge layers (hub.html:1252-1258).

pieces.name: Orb — the constellation orb
pieces.check: CHECK: color per category, fixed; hover lift 8px; tap opens the drill-down. Point values locked 2026-11-01.
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary orb: a glass planet in its own color, orbiting the gauge — molded to be a number you can touch, a door into its drill-down.
pieces.notes: Orb colors/points per Act §4.5 (Playbook map; CONFLICTS #17: live dashboard rotates Creating/Shares/Comments — the Act flags it, Shawn decides). Hub .orb rules harvested from hub.html directly; the earlier parts/frontend/orb-hub.css extract is cross-checked against the same rules.

pieces.name: Gauge — the instrument
pieces.check: CHECK: numeral angles exact by formula angle = -135 + (value/500)*270; all six numerals present (none skipped); ambient rotation 60–180s, active 18–25s, never under 12s; directions alternate; teeth, never solid rings.
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary gauge: the Bugatti instrument, numerals by formula, needle sweeping like acceleration — molded to give your score in 2 seconds.
pieces.notes: The gauge markup is JS-rendered (dashboard.html:20153-20311 builds .tn-tacho > .tn-tacho-dialwrap > svg.tn-tacho-dial); the specimen above copies that structure verbatim, content filled at build time. Full CSS is the tn-tacho block harvested here.

pieces.name: Smart app — the one app
pieces.check: CHECK: no second dashboard, no second mail, no second notes system — a duplicate is a fail.
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary app: one app, many doors, the same dashboard behind every door — molded so you never leave the machine, you only open more of it.
pieces.notes: ARCHITECTURAL PIECE — no separate CSS exists to harvest: the one app IS the shared shell behind every door. Its code is templates/*.html (Personal, Business, Space, Membership, Dashboard, Hub) + harvested/hub.html. Doors: Personal, Business, Space, Membership (Smart Access), Dashboard, Hub.

pieces.name: Page — a door
pieces.check: CHECK: one page at a time to finished; his eye verifies each before the next begins.
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary page: one door, one viewpoint, one purpose — molded to be a whole world with the standard kit inside.
pieces.notes: ARCHITECTURAL PIECE — the code is the template itself. Standard kit on every page (Act §4.8): Smart Mail + Instant Messenger, Smart Lists, Scheduler/Booker, About, products/services.

pieces.name: Section — a themed zone
pieces.check: CHECK: adjacent zones read as distinct (spectral order, never clumped).
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary section: one themed zone, one color, distinct from its neighbors — molded to be a room inside the world.
pieces.notes: NOTE: the precise boundary between section, page, and board is not defined in the sources (Act GAP #16) — reported, not invented.

pieces.name: Jewel — bullets are diamonds
pieces.check: CHECK: bullets are rotated squares, not dots; no color twice in a row.
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary jewel: bullets are diamonds, a cut stone that separates ideas — molded to be the color made physical, glowing even at rest.
pieces.notes: Five-jewel cycle in law order (hub.html:1300-1302: nth-child(5n+1..3) hot pink #ed42c4, purple #8a5cff, blue #3ca8ff — the diamond-bullet rule itself lives in piece 03 (hub.html:1273-1310, .ib-layer-body ul li::before: rotated square, own-color glow). Faceted-gem geometry: .v10-icon (piece 04).

pieces.name: Chart — the data display
pieces.check: CHECK: same materials and light as the gauge; 2-second test passed.
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary chart: the gauge’s other face, same materials, same light, same motion — molded to show the numbers so you understand your world in 2 seconds.

pieces.name: Tab / pill — the quiet element
pieces.check: CHECK: glows on hover. An element that does nothing on hover fails.
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary tab: the quiet element, dark at rest, glowing on hover without lifting — molded to switch a view without shouting.

pieces.name: Smart Link — the attested link
pieces.check: CHECK: a Smart Link carries its receipt (claim, verification, count).
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary link: a door with a receipt — SEE, VERIFY, confirm — molded to carry its claim, its verification, and its count.
pieces.notes: NOTE: its visual spec is not in the canon docs (Act GAP #17) — this harvest is the live dashboard rule only; the receipt (claim/verification/count) is a data requirement, not a style.

pieces.name: Header — the warm front door
pieces.check: CHECK: one clear line; full width.
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary header: the warm front door, logo + living mark + warm voice + one clear line, full width — molded to welcome in one line.
pieces.notes: Hub hero CSS lives inside a JS template literal (hub.html:6853-6886, st.textContent) — harvested verbatim as CSS text (lines 6857-6885; the literal closes on 6886); the .sh-hero markup is JS-rendered (hub.html:6795-6823).

pieces.name: Overlay — the top layer
pieces.check: CHECK: rides visibly above the control it serves; folds away when dismissed.
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary overlay: the top layer, a glass sheet riding above the board — molded to show the detail and fold away.

pieces.name: Control — the working element
pieces.check: CHECK: responds physically on touch; its state is visible.
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary control: the working element, a switch you can operate, its state visible — molded to take a person’s choice and show it.

pieces.name: Input — the well
pieces.check: CHECK: validation speaks plainly; nothing is saved when it shouldn't be; the well is recessed (inset shadow), not raised.
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary input: the well, a dark recessed channel you press INTO — molded to receive a person’s words and answer plainly.
pieces.notes: Hub Ask Naya well: hub.html:4584 renders <input type="search" id="chassisSearch" placeholder="Search your intelligence…">; its well styling is the .activity-search rule harvested here. Search lives BELOW the bar, never inside it (Act §4.17).

pieces.name: Case — the gauge body
pieces.check: CHECK: part of the gauge; the case is the housing everything else sits in. (Gauge CHECK §4.6 applies to the whole instrument.)
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary case: the housing everything sits in, obsidian, the body of the instrument — molded to hold the machine together.
pieces.notes: Sub-extract of the gauge (piece 06). Case = .tn-tacho housing + .tn-tacho-dialwrap.

pieces.name: Bezel — the machined edge
pieces.check: CHECK: the bezel frames the center; finish the outside. (Gauge CHECK §4.6 applies.)
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary bezel: machined aluminum, the edge the eye hits first — molded to frame the center.
pieces.notes: Brushed metal, machined aluminum (dashboard.html:2470 comment, Shawn 2026-11-01). .tn-bezel is a faceted SVG group; screws are .tn-bezel-screw.

pieces.name: Dial — the face
pieces.check: CHECK: numerals engraved on the aluminum ring, not floating; shadow offset (0.8px, 0.8px). (Gauge CHECK §4.6 applies.)
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary dial: the face, numerals engraved on aluminum, never floating — molded to be read at a glance.
pieces.notes: Black obsidian dial (dashboard.html:2443 comment). Numerals: Bugatti-style, etched on the metal (dashboard.html:2639 comment + rules in range).

pieces.name: Crystal — the glass
pieces.check: CHECK: light catching the glass as the machine settles. (Gauge CHECK §4.6 applies.)
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary crystal: real glass over the dial, light catching it as the machine settles — molded to prove it is glass, not a picture.
pieces.notes: Real glass with a visible reflection arc across the top (dashboard.html:2491 comment).

pieces.name: Needle — the value
pieces.check: CHECK: sweeps like acceleration; the number made physical. (Gauge CHECK §4.6 applies.)
pieces.craft: The most extraordinary needle: the value made physical, sweeping like acceleration, casting its shadow — molded to be the number you feel.
pieces.notes: Frame-driven for sync, sweeps like acceleration; casts a shadow — a physical object above the dial (dashboard.html:2553-2562).
